transcript.text: My name is Kevin Cooper and I'm the bear team leader, a burned area emergency response team leader for the Hertz Delta fire here in the Shash fraternity forest.
Just south of Mount Shash, the north of Reading here, up in these big watersheds and these foothills.
This late September we had this 70,000 acre fire that burned through all these trees here and now we're right up against the rainy season.
So we have to analyze the effects of what's going to happen when it starts raining. That's what the bear team does.

So we pull in this team of specialists to take a look at this and try to figure out when it rains, what's the increased probability of risk to life, property and critical cultural and natural resources.
The main players on the bear team are going to be the soil scientists who are looking at the changes in the soil because of the heat that's been parted to it.
And a hydrologist who's looking at the different soil moisture and the hydrogiology, where the water's moving, how deep it's going to be, how much is coming down the hills.
And then the geologist who's looking for debris flows and rock fall and things like that.
We have support staff like geographical information service, a GIS person who does a lot of the mapping.
We've got administrative assistant team leader like myself, road steam, looking at the roads, we've got a trail of recreation folks.
And we work with all the other agencies who have responsibilities outside this area too.
So natural resource conservation service, the other landowners, we work with NOAA weather who work with us with forecasting and warning systems.
And any other agencies like operations and emergency services in the counties and the state.
So it's a large group of people and everybody takes on their role and fills in their role and makes it safe for everybody if we all participate.
